overview.scoring: Каждая секция — балл 1–9 (шаг 0.5). Overall = среднее четырёх, округляется до ближайших 0.5.

bandMeaning.6: Компетентное — в целом эффективно, есть ошибки

typicalUniversityRequirements.bachelor: обычно 6.0–6.5 overall, не ниже 5.5–6.0 за секцию
typicalUniversityRequirements.master: обычно 6.5–7.0 overall, не ниже 6.0–6.5 за секцию
typicalUniversityRequirements.note: Точный порог всегда смотреть на странице программы. Топовые вузы и гуманитарные/юридические программы требуют 7.0–7.5.

criteria.Task Response: Полностью ответить на ВСЕ части вопроса, ясная позиция на протяжении всего эссе, идеи развиты и подкреплены примерами. Мин. 250 слов.
criteria.Coherence & Cohesion: Логика абзацев, один абзац — одна мысль, связки (however, moreover, as a result) уместны, есть вступление и вывод.
criteria.Lexical Resource: Разнообразная лексика, точная сочетаемость слов, синонимы вместо повторов, менее частотные слова к месту, минимум ошибок в написании.
criteria.Grammatical Range & Accuracy: Разные конструкции (сложноподчинённые, условные, пассив), большинство предложений без ошибок, верная пунктуация.

bandGuide.5: Отвечает на задание частично, позиция размытая; абзацы есть, но связки механические; лексики хватает лишь на базовые идеи, заметные ошибки; простые предложения преобладают, ошибки мешают.
bandGuide.6: Отвечает на все части, но неравномерно; позиция есть, вывод бывает нечёткий; связки местами избыточны/недостаточны; лексика адекватная, есть ошибки в словах; смесь простых и сложных предложений, ошибки не мешают пониманию.
bandGuide.7: Чётко отвечает на все части, ясная позиция всюду, идеи развёрнуты (иногда переобобщение); логичное развитие, хорошие связки; неплохой запас лексики, чувство стиля, редкие ошибки; много сложных предложений, большинство без ошибок.
bandGuide.8: Полный и точный ответ, идеи хорошо раскрыты; текст читается без усилий, абзацы выстроены; широкая и точная лексика, редкие оговорки; разнообразная грамматика, ошибки единичны.

questionTypes: Opinion (Agree/Disagree) — 'To what extent do you agree or disagree?'
Discussion (Both views) — 'Discuss both views and give your opinion.'
Advantages/Disadvantages — 'Do the advantages outweigh the disadvantages?'
Problem/Solution (Cause/Solution) — 'What are the problems and how can they be solved?'
Two-part question — два прямых вопроса в задании
writingTask2.essayStructure: Вступление (перефразировать тему + тезис) → Тело 1 (главная мысль + развитие + пример) → Тело 2 (вторая мысль + развитие + пример) → Вывод (повторить позицию). 4 абзаца, 260–290 слов.
practicePrompts: Some people think university education should be free for everyone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many young people today leave their home country to work abroad. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this trend.
Online learning is becoming more common. Do the benefits of studying online outweigh the drawbacks?
In many cities, traffic and pollution are serious problems. What causes this and what solutions can you suggest?
Some believe schools should teach practical skills like cooking and budgeting. Others think academic subjects matter more. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
International tourism brings money but can harm local culture. Do you think it is a positive or negative development?
Governments should invest more in public transport than in new roads. To what extent do you agree?
Children spend too much time on smartphones. What problems does this cause and how can parents address them?

Some believe that robots will eventually replace most human jobs. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Video games are becoming more realistic and popular among all age groups. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this trend.
Some think that governments should have the right to monitor people's internet activity for security reasons. To what extent do you agree?
Many people now prefer to communicate through text messages rather than face-to-face conversations. What problems does this cause and how can they be solved?
Some believe that technology has made children less creative and imaginative. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Self-driving cars are being tested in many cities. Do the advantages of this technology outweigh the disadvantages?
Some argue that people should be allowed to work from home permanently, while others think workplaces are essential. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
The use of facial recognition technology is increasing in public spaces. What are the benefits and drawbacks of this?
Some believe that reading news online has replaced reading printed newspapers entirely. Is this a positive or negative development?
Many people are concerned about the amount of personal data collected by technology companies. What problems does this cause and what solutions can be suggested?
Some think virtual reality will soon replace traditional classroom teaching. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
E-books have become more popular than printed books in recent years. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this trend.
Some argue that developing countries should focus on developing their own technology rather than importing it from richer nations. To what extent do you agree?

Many countries are shifting to renewable energy sources. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this change?
Some believe that a rise in the standard of living in a country results in a rise in environmental pollution. What are the causes and possible solutions?
Plastic packaging is a major cause of pollution. What problems does this cause and what solutions can you suggest?
Some argue that zoos are cruel and should be banned, while others believe they play an important role in conservation. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Deforestation is increasing rapidly in many parts of the world. What are the causes of this, and what measures can be taken to address it?
Some people think that a global tax on carbon emissions is the best way to fight climate change. To what extent do you agree?
Many species of animals are becoming endangered due to human activity. What can be done to protect them?

Some argue that governments should ban cars in city centres to reduce pollution. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
Fast fashion has a significant negative impact on the environment. What are the causes of this problem and how can it be solved?
Some think that environmental problems are too big to be solved by individual countries acting alone. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many cities are experiencing rising temperatures due to climate change. What problems does this cause and what solutions can be suggested?
Some believe that businesses should be responsible for the environmental damage they cause, rather than governments. To what extent do you agree?
The demand for meat is increasing worldwide, despite its environmental impact. Discuss the causes of this and possible solutions.
Some argue that eco-tourism helps protect the environment, while others think it does more harm than good. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Some believe that unpaid community service should be a compulsory part of high school programmes. To what extent do you agree?
Crime rates are rising in many big cities. What do you think are the causes, and what solutions can be suggested?
Some argue that voting in national elections should be made compulsory. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Some believe that prisons should focus on rehabilitating criminals rather than punishing them. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Corruption remains a serious problem in many countries. What are the causes of this and what can be done to reduce it?
Some believe that the media has too much influence over public opinion. To what extent do you agree?
Many cities are becoming overcrowded due to rapid urbanisation. What problems does this cause and how can they be solved?
Some argue that wealthy countries have a duty to help poorer countries develop. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Gender inequality persists in many workplaces around the world. What are the causes of this and what measures can be taken to address it?
Some think that the legal age for voting should be lowered to sixteen. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Immigration levels are rising in many developed countries. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
Some believe that governments should limit the number of children a family can have to control population growth. To what extent do you agree?
Homelessness remains a significant problem in many major cities. What are the causes of this and what solutions can be suggested?
Some argue that traditional customs and values are being lost as societies become more modern. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Public trust in politicians has declined in many countries. What are the causes of this, and what can be done to restore it?
Health: Fast food consumption is increasing worldwide. What are the causes and effects of this trend, and what solutions can you propose?
Some believe that people should exercise on their own, while others think joining a gym or team sport is more effective. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
The number of people suffering from stress-related illnesses is increasing. What do you think are the causes and possible solutions?
Some argue that governments should be responsible for people's health, while others believe individuals should take full responsibility. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Obesity rates are rising rapidly in many countries. What are the main causes of this problem and what solutions can be suggested?
Some believe that unhealthy foods such as sugary drinks should be taxed more heavily. To what extent do you agree?
Mental health problems among young people are increasing. What are the causes of this, and what can be done to address it?
Some think that healthcare should be free for everyone, regardless of income. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many people are turning to alternative medicine instead of conventional treatments. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
Some argue that advertising unhealthy food to children should be banned. To what extent do you agree?
The rise of sedentary lifestyles is a growing concern in modern society. What are the causes of this, and what solutions can be proposed?
Some believe that ageing populations will put unsustainable pressure on healthcare systems. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many countries are experiencing a shortage of doctors and nurses. What are the causes of this problem and how can it be solved?
Some think that people should be legally required to have regular health check-ups. To what extent do you agree?
Smoking rates have declined in many countries due to government campaigns. What further measures could help reduce smoking even more?
Some argue that social media has a negative effect on young people's mental health. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Sleep deprivation is becoming increasingly common in modern society. What are the causes of this, and what solutions can be suggested?
Some believe that vaccination should be made compulsory for all children. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Many workplaces now offer wellness programmes to support employee health. Do the benefits of this outweigh the costs?
Some think that food companies bear the most responsibility for rising obesity rates, while others blame individual choices. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Work & Economy: Automation is replacing many jobs previously done by humans. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
Some believe employees should have a fixed daily working schedule, while others prefer flexible hours. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
In many countries, young people change jobs more frequently than in the past. What are the reasons, and is this a positive or negative development?
Some think success in a career is mainly the result of hard work, while others believe it is mostly luck. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
Many companies now allow employees to work remotely full-time. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this trend?
Some argue that a four-day working week would benefit both employees and employers. To what extent do you agree?
The gap between the salaries of top executives and average workers is growing. What are the causes of this, and what should be done about it?

Unemployment among young graduates is rising in many countries. What are the causes of this problem and what solutions can be suggested?
Some think that large companies should be required to hire a certain percentage of local workers. To what extent do you agree?
Many people retire earlier than in the past due to better pensions. Do the advantages of early retirement outweigh the disadvantages?

Some believe that governments should raise the minimum wage significantly. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
Many young people today prefer to start their own businesses rather than work for established companies. What are the causes of this, and is it a positive development?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a person who influenced your choice of career.
questions: Do you think parents should choose careers for their children?
Why do some people change careers later in life?
Is job satisfaction more important than salary? Why?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a teacher who had a big influence on you.
questions: Why are some teachers more memorable than others?
Should teachers be strict or friendly with students?
How has the role of teachers changed with technology?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a famous person you would like to meet.
questions: Why are people so interested in the lives of celebrities?
Does fame bring more advantages or disadvantages to a person?
Should famous people feel obliged to be role models?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe someone who has achieved something significant in life.
questions: What does society usually consider to be a 'successful' person?
Do you think success is mostly about talent or hard work?
Should personal achievements always be recognised publicly?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a leader you admire (in your country or elsewhere).
questions: What qualities make someone a good leader?
Are leaders born with certain qualities, or can leadership be learned?
Is it harder to be a leader today than in the past?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a place you visited that you found relaxing.
questions: Why do you think people enjoy travelling to new places?
Is it better to travel alone or with other people?
How has tourism changed in your country over the last decade?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a city you would like to visit.
questions: What makes a city attractive to tourists?
Do you think cities around the world are becoming too similar to each other?
Is life in a big city better than life in the countryside?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a historical place you have visited or would like to visit.
questions: Why is it important to preserve historical places?
Should governments spend more money protecting historical sites?
How do historical places affect a country's sense of national identity?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a public place you like to spend time in.
questions: Why are public spaces important in a city?
Should governments invest more in parks and other public areas?
How have public spaces changed in your country in recent years?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a natural landscape that impressed you.
questions: Why do people often feel a strong connection to nature?
Should popular natural areas be protected from tourism?
How has urbanisation affected the natural environment in your country?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a piece of technology you find useful.
questions: How has technology changed communication between family members?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a gift you received that you liked.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe an invention you think is important.
questions: Which inventions do you think have changed daily life the most?

Should inventors receive more support and reward from governments?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe an old object that has been in your family for a long time.
questions: Why do people like to keep old family items?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a work of art you like.
questions: Why is art considered important in society?
Should governments fund art galleries and museums?
Has technology changed the way people experience art?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a memorable celebration or festival you attended.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a sporting event you watched or took part in.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe an event that brought your community together.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a graduation or important ceremony you attended.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a cultural event you attended.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a difficult decision you once made.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a skill you would like to learn.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a creative activity you like doing (art, music, writing, etc.).

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a film you enjoyed watching.

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a news story that interested you.
questions: How has the way people consume news changed in recent years?

Should there be stricter regulations for news published online?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a piece of music that means a lot to you.
questions: Why does music have such a strong effect on people's emotions?
Has music streaming changed how people discover new music?
Should music education be compulsory in schools?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a social media platform you use often.
questions: How has social media changed the way people communicate?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a goal you hope to achieve in the next five years.
questions: Why is it important for people to set goals?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a change you would like to make in your life.
questions: Why do people often find it difficult to change their habits?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a career goal you have.
questions: How do most people go about choosing their career path?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe a language you would like to learn.
questions: Why do people choose to learn a foreign language?

part3Sets.part2Topic: Describe an achievement you hope to be remembered for.
questions: What do most people want to be remembered for after they are gone?

Do you think future generations will define success differently than we do now?

studyPlan8Weeks.focus: Диагностика: пройти 1 полный бесплатный mock. Разобрать формат всех 4 секций. Завести словарь.
Listening: типы заданий, потренировать section 1–2. Reading: skimming/scanning, True/False/Not Given.
Writing Task 1 (Academic): язык описания трендов, 4 эссе по образцу. Speaking Part 1: записывать ответы на диктофон.
Writing Task 2: структура, 3 типа вопросов, 3 эссе + самопроверка по дескрипторам. Learn 50 topic-collocations.
Listening section 3–4 (лекции). Reading: matching headings, gap-fill. Mid-check mock (Listening+Reading).
Writing Task 2: оставшиеся типы вопросов, 4 эссе, работа над Coherence. Speaking Part 2: 10 cue cards, таймер.
Полный mock под таймер. Speaking Part 3: развёрнутые ответы. Точечно закрыть слабую секцию.
2 полных mock с проверкой. Повторить словарь и связки. За 2 дня до экзамена — только лёгкое повторение.
